concepts_present.evidence_quote: We introduce a Region Proposal Network (RPN) that shares full-image convolutional features with the detection network.
We introduce novel 'anchor' boxes that serve as references at multiple scales and aspect ratios.
Faster R-CNN is composed of two modules: a deep fully convolutional network that proposes regions, and the Fast R-CNN detector that uses the proposed regions.
We adopt non-maximum suppression on the proposal regions based on their cls scores.
RoI pooling layer ... The ROI pooling layer uses max pooling to convert the features inside any valid region of interest into a small feature map.
Our loss function for an image is defined as ... a multi-task loss with classification log loss and bounding-box regression.
We achieve state-of-the-art object detection accuracy on PASCAL VOC 2007, 2012, and MS COCO datasets.

concepts_absent.rationale: Faster R-CNN is the canonical anchor-based detector; it explicitly motivates the introduction of anchors.
Faster R-CNN uses NMS to deduplicate, not bipartite matching or set prediction.
Architecture is fully convolutional + RPN; no transformer.
Faster R-CNN uses cross-entropy without the focal modulation term.
Faster R-CNN is detection-only; the mask branch is added later by Mask R-CNN.
ROIAlign is a Mask R-CNN contribution; Faster R-CNN uses RoIPool with quantization.
Compound scaling is an EfficientDet contribution and not part of Faster R-CNN.
Faster R-CNN replaces external Selective Search with the integrated RPN, motivated explicitly by SS being the speed bottleneck.
Faster R-CNN is a deep-learning detector; DPM is a classical part-based method not used in this architecture.
Features are learned by VGG/ResNet backbones; no HOG/SIFT-style hand-engineered features.
